title: GraphQL query-cost limits must count fields and aliases inside inline fragments and fragment spreads
answers: GraphQL query exceeds MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ROOT_FIELDS but still runs
alias limit bypassed by putting aliases inside ... on Query or a named fragment
check_query_safety does not reject fragment-wrapped root fields
body:
Symptom: A GraphQL request with more root fields or aliases than MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ROOT_FIELDS / MAX_ALIASES allows is executed when the extra fields sit inside an inline fragment or a named fragment spread.
Root cause: mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py:scan_query only iterated direct FieldNode children, so InlineFragmentNode and FragmentSpreadNode selections were skipped.
Fix pattern: Expand fragments before counting. _collect_fields_and_aliases flattens inline fragments and spreads (resolved via a fragment_defs map built from FragmentDefinitionNode) into the same level, then scan_query counts root_fields and aliases from that flattened list.
Constraints: Fragment definitions are only used through spreads reachable from an OperationDefinitionNode; unused fragments are not counted. Any new selection-node type added to GraphQL traversal must be handled in _collect_fields_and_aliases or it reopens this bypass.
applies: Applies to the query-cost scanner in mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py; not to the GraphQL schema or resolvers.
says: API query complexity limits are bypassed when requests wrap fields in fragments.
Requests exceeding allowed field and alias counts still execute instead of being rejected.
Enforce server query size restrictions on nested and spread definitions across API calls.
Why does the backend permit expensive queries with hidden aliases inside fragment blocks?

Unused fragment definitions are not counted, and any new selection-node type in GraphQL traversal must be handled in _collect_fields_and_aliases. Applies to the query-cost scanner in mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py, not to the GraphQL schema or resolvers.
